title: Pressure, floating and the ocean of air
scope: Choose the objectives in your school’s topic list. These are original practice questions with illustrative values, not a claim of an official school paper format.

objectives.label: Explain and use pressure.
objectives.note: Pressure is normal force per unit area.

objectives.label: Explain and use atmospheric pressure.
objectives.note: Air pressure results from molecular collisions, and atmospheric pressure changes with the overlying atmosphere.

objectives.label: Explain and use pressure difference.
objectives.note: A difference in pressure can produce a net force and drive fluid motion.

objectives.label: Explain and use hydrostatic pressure change.
objectives.note: In a uniform liquid at rest, pressure increases with depth by density × gravitational field strength × depth change.

objectives.label: Explain and use density and floating.
objectives.note: Density is mass per volume; a freely floating object displaces a weight of fluid equal to its own weight.

cards.definition: Pressure is normal force per unit area.
cards.explanation: Use the relationship in the stated conditions and name the objects or system being considered.
cards.example: A model support must limit pressure to 2400 Pa while supporting a uniform normal force of 96 N. Calculate the minimum contact area. Area = normal force ÷ pressure. 96 ÷ 2400 = 0.040 m²; a smaller area would exceed the pressure limit.
cards.confusion: A larger total force need not mean a larger pressure if the area also changes.
cards.question: Explain pressure from memory. What common mistake must you avoid?
cards.answer: Pressure is normal force per unit area. A larger total force need not mean a larger pressure if the area also changes.

cards.definition: Air pressure results from molecular collisions, and atmospheric pressure changes with the overlying atmosphere.
cards.explanation: Use the relationship in the stated conditions and name the objects or system being considered.
cards.example: Why does atmospheric pressure usually decrease as you climb a mountain? There is less atmosphere above you. The smaller weight of overlying air requires a smaller pressure to support it.
cards.confusion: Air can exert a force even when it is invisible or apparently still.
cards.question: Explain atmospheric pressure from memory. What common mistake must you avoid?
cards.answer: Air pressure results from molecular collisions, and atmospheric pressure changes with the overlying atmosphere. Air can exert a force even when it is invisible or apparently still.

cards.definition: A difference in pressure can produce a net force and drive fluid motion.
cards.explanation: Use the relationship in the stated conditions and name the objects or system being considered.
cards.example: A suction cup sticks to a smooth tile when its internal pressure is reduced. What supplies the net holding force? The greater outside air pressure pushes the cup towards the tile. The smaller internal pressure provides a smaller opposing force.
cards.confusion: “Suction” does not mean an empty space pulls fluid towards itself.
cards.question: Explain pressure difference from memory. What common mistake must you avoid?
cards.answer: A difference in pressure can produce a net force and drive fluid motion. “Suction” does not mean an empty space pulls fluid towards itself.

cards.definition: In a uniform liquid at rest, pressure increases with depth by density × gravitational field strength × depth change.
cards.explanation: Use the relationship in the stated conditions and name the objects or system being considered.
cards.example: Pressure increases by 7200 Pa between two points in still fresh water. Use density 1000 kg/m³ and g = 10 N/kg. Calculate their vertical depth difference. Depth difference = pressure increase ÷ (density × g). 7200 ÷ (1000 × 10) = 0.72 m.
cards.confusion: Depth matters; total width or volume alone does not set pressure at a given depth.
cards.question: Explain hydrostatic pressure change from memory. What common mistake must you avoid?
cards.answer: In a uniform liquid at rest, pressure increases with depth by density × gravitational field strength × depth change. Depth matters; total width or volume alone does not set pressure at a given depth.

cards.definition: Density is mass per volume; a freely floating object displaces a weight of fluid equal to its own weight.
cards.explanation: Use the relationship in the stated conditions and name the objects or system being considered.
cards.example: A sealed floating block is moved from fresh water to denser salt water. Will it float higher or lower? Explain. It floats higher. A smaller displaced volume of the denser fluid has the same weight needed to balance the block’s weight.
cards.confusion: The material alone does not determine an object’s average density when it contains air.
cards.question: Explain density and floating from memory. What common mistake must you avoid?
cards.answer: Density is mass per volume; a freely floating object displaces a weight of fluid equal to its own weight. The material alone does not determine an object’s average density when it contains air.
